deep_dive.title: The Case for Automated Hyperspecialization: Evidence from SAT
deep_dive.abstract: The software status quo is to use one system to process many different kinds of inputs. In contrast, we propose hyperspecialization: creating new software that is optimized for a single class of inputs. Hyperspecializing manually is anywhere from expensive to impossible. We conjecture that coding agents make automated hyperspecialization cheap, effective, and safe for problems with measurable performance and checkable output. This paper explores one such problem, SAT solving, by synthesizing hundreds of workload-specific SAT solvers at an average cost of \$37 each. Our specialists outperform their competition-winning, general-purpose cousins by 5$\times$ on average, and by over $10\times$ on a quarter of benchmark families. A general-purpose solver constructed from over a hundred of our prototype hyperspecialists won the SAT track at the 2026 SAT Competition.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Manually building specialized software is costly, so the authors use coding agents to auto-synthesize hundreds of workload-specific SAT solvers for about $37 each, outperforming general-purpose winners by 5x on average and over 10x on a quarter of families.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 现有软件通常用一套通用系统处理各类输入，但为单一输入类定制软件成本高、难度大。本文提出“超特化”思路，利用编码智能体自动为不同工作负载合成专用 SAT 求解器，平均每个仅需约 37 美元。实验表明这些专用求解器平均比获奖的通用求解器快 5 倍，在四分之一的基准族上快逾 10 倍。该工作证明大语言模型驱动的自动代码生成可廉价且有效地实现 SAT 求解器定制化设计。
